title: Microflow Loom: catalog and synthetic dry-run for admin utilities
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight catalog and synthetic dry-run harness (Microflow Loom) that converts existing runbook fragments and shortflows into idempotent, typed microflows developers and oncall can execute safely. The goal is to reduce friction for first-line responders by surfacing curated, parameterized microflows, enabling local dry-runs against sanitized fixtures, and capturing provenance for audit and telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog UI endpoint that lists microflow metadata and required params
Dry-run engine that executes flows against sandboxed fixtures without mutating production resources
Microflows are compiled to idempotent step sequences with replay tokens and timeouts
Telemetry events emitted for run start/finish, step durations, and dry-run diffs
Security gating: RBAC check and KMS usage pattern documented and enforced
Integration tests covering 3 canonical admin scenarios and one failure injection
tasks: spec: define microflow manifest schema and parameter typing
ingest: write adapters to convert 10 high-priority runbook fragments into manifests
dryrun: implement synthetic execution harness using fixtures and network fakes
ui: add /internal/microflows catalog API and minimal console page
telemetry: add events and dashboard quicklinks (latency, success rate, dry-run vs live)
security: run RBAC review and KMS integration checklist
qa: create smoke harness and 3 scenario tests for CI
comments: 2025-02-16: Kickoff — scoped MVP to catalog+dry-run; will not run live remediations for MVP. Agreed to use fixture layer rather than full sandboxed infra.
2025-02-21: Architecture sync — decided microflow manifests will be YAML-first with strong typing for params and an optional 'safety-mode' tag. Miguel to prototype manifest -> stepgraph compiler.
2025-02-24: Design review — UX suggests compact parameter forms with example templates; link to Figma: https://redwood.design/f/microflow-loom-proto (internal)
2025-02-28: Engineering update — prototype dry-run harness can replay steps against mocked API adapters; observed a race in KV-cache clears, added step-level locking to manifest runtime.
2025-03-01: PR opened — https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-tooling/pull/482 (microflow manifest schema + compiler prototype). Requesting review from @sarah-chen and @devops-team.
2025-03-03: PM feedback — include success/error examples for each microflow in the catalog and mark ones safe-for-oncall. Miguel to add metadata flags.
notes: Rationale: many runbook fragments are brittle to run manually; compiling them to typed microflows improves reproducibility and enables safe automation later.
Tradeoffs: using synthetic fixtures reduces fidelity vs full sandbox but accelerates shipping and removes cost/permission blockers for early usage.
Follow-ups: add live-preview mode with throttled, audited remediations in a later phase (post MVP).
